Now be a good courier and deliver it!|{restraining anger, losing it a little towards end} }}|sound=FNV RobertHouse BeAGoodCourier.ogg}} }} '''Robert Edwin House''', typically known as '''Mr. House''', is the enigmatic ruler of [[New Vegas]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]]. Prior to the [[Great War]], House was the founder and CEO of [[RobCo Industries]], who used life-preservation [[technology]] to survive the bombs from within the [[Lucky 38]]. He later emerged from hibernation to become the self-styled president, CEO and sole proprietor of the [[New Vegas Strip]], uniting various [[Tribals|tribes]] and using his [[securitron]]s to form the post-War city-state of the [[Free Economic Zone of New Vegas]] by [[Timeline#2281|2281]]. House appears as a central character {{in|FNV}} who can facilitate one of the game's major [[Fallout: New Vegas endings|endings]]. His [[Robert House's double|body double]] appears in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'']] TV series' [[Fallout TV series season 1|first season]], and he fully appears in its [[Fallout TV series season 2|second season]] in a more prominent role. The pre-War House also appears in ''[[Fallout Shelter]]''. ==Background== {{Quotation|Robert House is an enigmatic, all-powerful technocrat dedicated to the pursuit of his own interests, by any means necessary.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ===Pre-War=== Robert House was born on June 25, [[Timeline#2020|2020]],[[A tragedy has befallen all mankind]] and grew up around [[New Vegas|Las Vegas]], Nevada,The [[Courier]]: ''"What was Vegas like before the war?"''
Robert House: ''"It was a place of splendor. As magnificent as today's Strip may seem, it's but a shadow of the neon paradise that was Las Vegas. I grew up not far from here, and though I traveled the old world extensively, I never found another place like it."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) but was orphaned at the age of two when his parents died in a freak accident involving an autogyro and a lightning strike. Cheated out of his inheritance by his half-brother, [[Anthony House|Anthony]],''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide]] Collectors Edition'' p.305: ''"[2.06] H&H Tools Factory''
''Long before the war, H&H Tools Company provided Nevada and California high-quality robotics equipment. Owned by the half-brother of Robert Edwin House (the founder of RobCo, and—were it not for the 200 year gap—the same man who lives in the Lucky 38 Casino). When their father was killed in an accident, the elder brother swindled Robert out of the family fortune, and assumed control of the company.''
''Robert went on, through his dealings with RobCo and their lucrative contracts, to become one of the wealthiest men on earth. His half-brother meanwhile, became increasingly paranoid, seeking to guard himself against a vengeance that never came, and inflicting all manner of strange HR rules on his workforce. The remains of this factory still stand, surrounded by husk-like remains of North Vegas' industrial area."''
([[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland]]) he nevertheless managed to achieve attendance to the [[The Institute|Commonwealth Institute of Technology]] and later went on to found [[RobCo Industries]] in 2042, at the age of 22. Under Robert's leadership, it soon became one of the most profitable corporations in the world, which House credited mostly to his own technical genius and business acumen. Whatever the case, House's success led to him being regarded by his peers with envy, by the public as a "genius" and a "captain of industry," and by the tabloids as the nation's most infamously eccentric businessman.The [[Courier]]: ''"Can you tell me anything about Mr. House?"''
[[Raul Tejada]]: ''"Just how old do you think I am, boss? Because I can pretty much guarantee I'm older than that. Let me tell you a story from before the Great War: Everybody knew Robert House. He was a genius. A superstar. Founded RobCo at 22, dated Hollywood starlets, the works. They say he saved Las Vegas. I was in Mexico City when the bombs dropped. Even from there, we could see House's defensive rockets shooting down the incoming missiles. Everybody assumed he died in the War. Maybe he did. But his robots are still out there, roaming the Wastes. And now, a Mr. House rules New Vegas."''
([[RaulTejada.txt|Raul Tejada's dialogue]])The [[Courier]]: ''"What's your opinion of Mr. House?"''
[[Beatrix Russell]]: ''"Before or after the human race shot itself in the foot? I been around long enough to have both opinions, see. Before the war, Mr. House was a famous captain of industry - robotics, to be specific. Seemed charming in interviews, until he became a recluse. Since the war, though? Didn't make a peep for near two hundred years - but when he came back, he came back strong and killed a lot of people."''

Sad times, indeed.|Still nostalgic, then a little sad at the end.}} The company really took off when RobCo purchased REPCONN in late 2076 to develop unmanned rockets to explore the solar system."''
([[REPCONTourGuide.txt|Tour guide's dialogue]]) the [[Lucky 38|Lucky 38 Hotel & Casino]] on [[New Vegas Strip|Las Vegas Boulevard]], and the [[H&H Tools Company]], the family business that would have been his before being usurped by his half-brother (although the factory on the outskirts of Vegas was still under the elder House's control in [[Timeline#2077|2077]]).[[Lucky 38 VIP keycard]] Feeling a deep love for his home city and wishing to bring it into his vision as a city of "luxury without decadence, refinement without elitism, [and] class without snobbery,"''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland|Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide]]'' Collector's Edition p.341-343: ''"Lucky 38"
The towering superstructure of the Lucky 38, which has been the base of operations for Mr. House for as long as anyone can remember (even the non-feral Ghouls), the giant monolith seems more like a well-maintained mausoleum of Pre-War Vegas glory once you enter. Though it is not an active casino, it is an enduring monument to Mr. House's vision of Las Vegas: luxury without decadence, refinement without elitism, class without snobbery. This is still the ultimate lure of Vegas: the one that tells anyone that they too could be a winner, just like Mr. House. Even with multiple wings and floors shut off, the rare visitors that enter the premises soon understand that the Lucky 38 is enormous.
This is the most prominent location in the Mojave Wasteland skyline, and should be used to situate yourself when wandering. Waiting outside the foot of the giant tower is Victor, who cheerfully beckons you in the first (and subsequent) times you visit.'' However, along with Robert's fame came public scrutiny over elements of his peculiar personality. A minor scandal emerged when House dated a [[Hollywood]] starlet but only spent their private time scanning her brain and making her dress in different outfits, a story that captured the interest of foreign tabloids like ''[[El Periódico de las Aburridas]]''.The [[Courier]]: ''"Maybe there's a connection. The Courier: ''"That's sickening."''
Raul Tejada: ''"It was quite the scandal, at least in the Latin-American tabloid journalism market."''
([[RaulTejada.txt|Raul Tejada's dialogue]]) Despite being a highly public figure, House chose to remain highly reclusive, employing a [[Robert House's double|body double]] to represent him in all public appearances,{{FOTV|2|5}} to the point that House himself was not widely recognized when he appeared in public.{{FOTV|2|1}} Another use of House's time while running his company was regularly designing and running mathematical paradigms based on global political and socioeconomic conditions in an effort to predict future events. By April 14, [[Timeline#2065|2065]], at 5:17 a.m., these projections led him to the inexorable conclusion that the world would be engulfed in a nuclear war within fifteen years. This was, to him, a mathematical certainty, and it led him to seek preparations.The [[Courier]]: ''"You say that you saved Las Vegas. How?"''
Robert House: ''"By 2065 I deemed it a mathematical certainty that an atomic war would devastate the Earth within 15 years. Every projection I ran confirmed it. I knew I couldn't "save the world," nor did I care to. But I could save Vegas, and in the process, perhaps, save mankind. I set to work immediately. I thought I had plenty of time to prepare. As it turned out, I was 20 hours short."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]])[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"You said you knew everything."''
Robert House: ''"I routinely design and run mathematical paradigms based on global, political, and socioeconomic conditions in an effort to... predict future events. And one spring morning, the data coalesced, and it told me, in no uncertain terms, that the world would... well, end."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Calculator told you that?"''
Robert House: ''"The date of the end of the world may not interest you, Mr. Howard. But the date the data coalesced might. April 14th, 2065, at 5:17 a.m. Is that date of any interest to you?"''
Cooper Howard: ''"That's my daughter's birthday."''
Robert House: ''"Oh, that is vexingly curious, isn't it? More curious is that you were not meant to come to Vegas this weekend. Your wife Barbara was meant to come alone. The moment that you bought your ticket to Las Vegas, the date the world was going to end... jumped forward by one month."''
Cooper Howard: ''"What are you, a f-fortune teller now?"''
Robert House: ''"I am a mathematician, a roboticist, and a casino owner. And I don't know yet how you figure into all of this, but you most certainly do. And I don't like unknown variables. Irksome. Not knowing exactly how you play a part in ending the world."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) ====Preparing for the war==== {{Quotation|Like yourself, [[The Ghoul|Mr. Howard]], I am an apex competitor. We are the very best at what we do. And what I do, is I know everything.|House to [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] in "[[The Wrangler]]"}} Armed with his knowledge of the coming war, House devoted the next twelve years making preparations to ensure his home city would survive the apocalypse and that he would live to see the world after the war. While the primary goal of his countermeasures was to disable incoming nuclear warheads by remotely transmitting disarm codes, House included contingencies for directly destroying any that managed to get through using laser detonations and defensive missiles or rockets.The [[Courier]]: ''"What preparations did you make to save Las Vegas?"''
Robert House: ''"On the day of the Great War, 77 atomic warheads targeted Las Vegas, [[Hoover Dam]], and its surrounding areas. My networked mainframes were able to predict and force-transmit disarm code subsets to 59 warheads, neutralizing them before impact. Laser cannons mounted on the roof of the Lucky 38 destroyed another 9 warheads. The rest got through, though none hit the city itself. A sub-optimal performance, admittedly. If only the Platinum Chip had arrived a day sooner..."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) House also acted to prevent other factions from taking over Vegas: though he allowed Vault-Tec to build a [[Las Vegas management Vault|specialized management Vault]] underneath the city, he also sabotaged it to ensure it would not be able to serve its intended purpose. House took equally drastic steps to preserve his own life: biologically, House planned to place his physical body within a [[Life support chamber|life-support device]], removing House's physical presence but wiring his brain directly into his vast information network via an enormous supercomputer to ensure he could continue to influence the world after the bombs.The [[Courier]]: ''"You appear to be a computer, not a man."''
Robert House: ''"Don't let the video screens and computer terminals fool you. I'm flesh and blood, not silicon."''
The Courier: ''"The lifespan you're claiming is impossible, except for ghouls and super mutants."''
Robert House: ''"[SUCCEEDED] I see you've made a study of the topic. My knowledge of the science of longevity would fill several text books... Perhaps, after a decade or two of economic reconstruction, I can commercialize these technologies and offer to others, such as yourself."''
The Courier: ''"How have you stayed alive all this time?"''
Robert House: ''"Let's just say it was very... {{Tooltip|costly|beat}}. But I was willing to make the sacrifices longevity entailed, financial and otherwise."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]])[[Lucky 38 terminal entries#Terminal (control room)|Lucky 38 terminal entries; control room terminal, Disable Cerebral Interface]] As another plan, House also sought to develop a [[Artificial personality|digitized version of his consciousness]] through his brain scanning technology which would persist in his supercomputer network, though this would require an immensely powerful energy source. He also worked to acquire any and all technologies that he considered relevant to his plans, while also using his unique position to continue collecting any and all knowledge of the key situations in the world.Robert House: ''"Like yourself, Mr. Howard, I am an apex competitor. We are the very best at what we do. And what I do, is I know everything. I know who is making what technology, and I acquire that technology at the most lucrative moment in its span of functionality. This week, I'm acquiring Cold Fusion from Vault-Tec."''
[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"From my wife."''
Robert House: ''"Correct. It will allow me to stay alive indefinitely in roboticized, non-biological form and protect Las Vegas from the coming nuclear war."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Initiated by my wife."''
Robert House: ''"Hmm. Unclear."''
Cooper Howard: ''"By Vault-Tec, then?"''
Robert House: ''"No, I doubt that, despite what we've both heard in that meeting. Vault-Tec is a collision of bureaucrats. Your wife, though... I don't know."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) Sometime during the [[Battle of Anchorage]], House gained access to the [[T-45 power armor]] worn by [[United States Marine Corps|U.S. Marine]] [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] via a piece of software he had licensed to [[West Tek]]. Through this, House was able to observe the situation on the [[Alaska]]n frontline, including Cooper's encounter with a "[[Deathclaw (TV series)|demon in the snow]]." House recognized that this "demon" was a piece of biotechnology developed by some unknown party, and came to believe that this was heavily intertwined with the future of the United States, as well as to Vault-Tec through Cooper's wife [[Barb Howard]], a high-ranking Vault-Tec executive.Robert House: ''"Mr. Howard, I was there with you in Alaska."''
[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"I doubt that very much."''
Robert House: ''"Not physically, of course. I'm not insane. But I did license a piece of software to West Tek, which gave me access to the T-45 Armor you wore. So, I saw what you saw. I saw it all. I saw the demon in the snow. And I believe that it's connected to the future of this great nation. And to your wife."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) Whether or not he had realized by then, House eventually came to recognize that Cooper Howard was heavily involved in the Great War according to his projections: in fact, the very date that his data coalesced around the prediction of nuclear war, April 14, 2065, was the date that Cooper and Barb's daughter [[Janey Howard|Janey]] was born. This was House's first indication that he was not the only one planning to survive and take power after the war, though he would not fully recognize this until much later on. Later in the 2070s, House and RobCo Industries developed a [[brain-computer interface chip]], which possessed mind control capabilities. House himself conducted a field test of the chip in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]] on a construction worker named [[Bill (TV series)|Bill]], successfully ordering the man to attack and kill his friends. Although the field test went awry when House cranked up the power of the chip using a remote control device, causing Bill's head to explode, House still saw it as remarkable progress. By 2077, House had instead set his sights on a different technology: Vault-Tec's proprietary [[cold fusion diode]], which he intended to use to power his digitized consciousness backup. House brokered a deal with Vault-Tec's leadership to trade his brain-computer control chip technology in exchange for the cold fusion diode, which he would then receive from Barb Howard during a defense contractors' summit in Las Vegas later in the year.[[Robert House's double]]: ''"RobCo presents the automated man. Spent a lot of time trying to make my machines more lifelike, but, hey, works the other way around, too."''
[[Barb Howard]]: ''"Mr. House, Vault-Tec and RobCo have always had a special arrangement. You have multiple Vaults to do with as you wish. If this is the research you'd like to pursue in the Vaults, you--"''
Robert House's double: ''"You must have missed the telegram. You're paying me for this. In exchange, I get Cold Fusion to power my little project in Vegas."''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) [[File:Robert House TV series.png|thumb|left|200px|Robert House's body double attending the meeting]] That same year, not long after informing Barb Howard of his deal for cold fusion, House was invited to a secret Vault-Tec meeting led by Barb Howard and [[Bud Askins]], also attended by American corporate representatives Frederick Sinclair, [[Julia Masters]], and [[Leon Von Felden]], where Barb Howard indicated Vault-Tec was willing to detonate the bombs themselves to ensure their profits. However, House did not trust these figures or their plans, merely sending his body double to the meeting, whom he used via earpiece to call out the plan's flaws. Viewing the plan as unsound from the very start, House came to believe that none of the figures present, nor Vault-Tec itself, would be the ones to launch the bombs. Instead, he suspected that the war would be caused by a hidden party -- the same one which created the "demon in the snow" he had seen in Alaska. He feared that this other entity was also making plans to outlast the war, and that they would ultimately claim victory over his plans given how successfully they had hidden their existence from him.[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"You know, the person who wanted me to kill you, you know what they think? They think that you are gonna end things by selling Vault-Tec the weapons it needs."''
Robert House: ''"No. The bombs will not be dropped by me or any of the idiots at that meeting. What I believe... I believe there is a... another player at the table. The same unknown entity responsible for your demon in the snow."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Who?"''
Robert House: ''"I don't know. It's like I said. Irksome. As you see, I live my life by one simple maxim."''
Cooper Howard: ''"The House always wins, right?"''
Robert House: ''"And it does. I'm making sure of it using every single piece of technology at my disposal. But what if I'm not the House? What if someone else is?"''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) =====The cold fusion deal===== Barb Howard's trip to Las Vegas, during which she would deliver the cold fusion diode to House, was set to take place not long after this meeting. However, [[Lee Moldaver|Kate Williams]], the inventor of this cold fusion technology, had been tracking Vault-Tec's plans due to her seeming suspicion that Vault-Tec intended to start nuclear war, and she somehow acquired the details of House's trade for cold fusion. She concluded that House was working with Vault-Tec and would give them the weapons that would enable them to kick-start nuclear war in exchange for the cold fusion diode, and subsequently convinced Cooper Howard to visit Las Vegas alongside his wife to assassinate Robert House and retrieve the cold fusion diode. This quickly caught House's attention, as his predictions indicated that Barb was supposed to come to the meeting alone; as soon as Cooper bought his ticket, his predicted date for the occurrence of nuclear war jumped forward by one month, indicating that Cooper was also an unknown variable of interest. To scope out Cooper, House visited an [[American Veteran Entertainment Alliance]] awards ceremony in Los Angeles ahead of Barb's trip, posing as a civilian to get a sense of Cooper's loyalties and beliefs.{{FOTV|2|3}} Subsequently, when Cooper arrived to the Lucky 38 during Barb's trip, House took the opportunity to call Cooper directly to his penthouse, where he revealed that he knew why Cooper had come; that they both knew about the "demon in the snow" and Vault-Tec's conspiracy; that he considered Cooper a significant person of interest for his influence over House's calculations of nuclear war; and that he believed some other party -- the same one which created the "demon in the snow" -- would ultimately be responsible for dropping the nukes. Cooper rejected House's claims, calling him a lunatic; House in turn derided Cooper as a "killer" and possibly the one who directly would end the world as Cooper left.[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"What if you're just a fucking lunatic?"''
Robert House: ''"I'm a lunatic?"''
Cooper Howard: ''"Yeah."''
Robert House: ''"I would encourage you to gaze inward, Mr. Howard, to your small life, spending your days pretending to be a cowboy, while your wife is making apocalyptic proposals at board meetings, and I'm building a missile system to defend this glorious city from what's coming. ({{FOTV|2|8}}) {{Small|This is House's phone call to Cooper at [[Camp McCarran|McCarran International Airport]].}} ===The Great War=== Though the loss of the cold fusion diode ruined House's ability to use his non-biological backup plan, he was still able to preserve himself biologically inside the Lucky 38. However, House still could not guarantee the successful execution of his plans without one key item: the [[platinum chip]], a computer chip containing a vital OS upgrade for his Securitrons and the Las Vegas anti-missile laser defense network. The chip was to be delivered to him in the afternoon of October 23, 2077. However, a miscalculation of mere hours by House prevented its arrival in time.The [[Courier]]: ''"Why didn't the Platinum Chip arrive on time?"''

([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) 20 hours before the chip's scheduled delivery, the [[Great War]] occurred, resulting in the chip being lost in the ruins for the next 200 years. Forced to work with an inferior OS, House endured numerous system crashes but was still able to protect Las Vegas from most, though not all, of the nuclear warheads aimed at the city. The strain on his systems nearly killed him, but House managed to survive.The [[Courier]]: ''"How did you nearly die, defending Vegas?"''
Robert House: ''"Software glitches set off a cascade of system crashes. I had to take the Lucky 38's reactor offline, lest it melt down. For nearly five years I battled power outages and more system crashes until I finally managed to reboot my data core with an older version of the OS. I spent the next few decades in a veritable coma. But I survived, obviously - and eventually thrived."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) He spent the next five years struggling against power outages and frequent crashes until he rebooted his data core with a downgraded version of his software. This left House in a coma for the next several decades, allowing the remains of Vegas to be picked over by the people of the surrounding wasteland. ===Post-War=== ====Creating New Vegas==== {{quotation|Mr. House is the mysterious overlord of the Strip. He controls his small empire from the confines of the Lucky 38 casino, where no other living person has set foot for over two hundred years.|[[Loading screen]]}} [[file:The House Always Wins.jpg|right|thumb|House in his penthouse, a sight very few were privy to.]] House regained consciousness from his coma in [[Timeline#2138|2138]].''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide]] Collector's Edition'' p.454: ''"2138: Mr. House regains consciousness."''
([[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide/Behind the Bright Lights & Big City]]) Instead of immediately revealing himself, he opted to stay hidden and wait for signs of an organized civilization having returned. Eventually, he entered the world stage once again in 2274, when [[Securitron]]s under his command emerged from the [[Lucky 38]]. This action was prompted by the detection of [[New California Republic]] scouts arriving at [[Hoover Dam]]. In order to establish his rule, House enlisted the help of three of the [[Tribals|tribes]] who had descended from [[Vault]] dwellers and were now living in the Las Vegas ruins.[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide]] Collector's Edition p.42: ''"Freeside"''
''"Las Vegas wasn't heavily damaged during the Great War, but people didn't immediately "settle" into the remnants of the old city. The various Vault tribes that emerged years later, hunted and fought among the ruins, but it was not until the "return" of Mr. House that they ceased (most) of their hostilities. Mr House directed the tribes to use his sizable quantities of pre-war construction materials to build the crude (but effective) outer walls that separate The Strip and Freeside from the rest of New Vegas. While Mr. House valued the area around Fremont Street, he ultimately viewed it as secondary in importance to the Strip itself and he had a second, inner wall that separated the two areas. When NCR prospectors (and eventually the army) arrived in the region, people typically went straight for The Strip, leaving Freeside (as it had become known by locals) as an informal stopping point. Eventually Mr. House recognized that he could use Freeside as a filter for undesirables, and pulled his favored tribes and all Securitrons into the Strip, leaving Freeside to fend for itself."''
([[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide faction profiles]]) These three tribes became the [[Three Families]]: the [[Chairmen]], the [[Omertas]], and the [[White Glove Society]]. Under House's guidance, they forced out all of their rivals and rebuilt the [[New Vegas Strip]], establishing the [[Free Economic Zone of New Vegas]] and accepting House's rule as its president, CEO and sole proprietor. Those forced out of the Strip were left to fend for themselves in surrounding areas such as what would later become [[Freeside]]; House purposefully left these areas alone, realizing that they were useful filters for people he did not want on the Strip.[[Courier]]: ''"How have the Khans been kicked around?"''
[[Yes Man]]: ''"They were one of the tribes the Three Families pushed out of Vegas! A whole bunch got killed! So they settled at Bitter Springs, but they kept being so obnoxious, the NCR had to kill a whole bunch more of them! So then they settle at Red Rock Canyon! There's just no getting rid of them!"''
([[VMQTopsYesMan.txt|Yes Man's dialogue]])The [[Courier]]: ''"How did the Three Families defeat you?"''
[[Papa Khan]]: ''"They allied with Mr. House, the self-proclaimed master of New Vegas. He supported them with the resources of New Vegas: weapons, technology, caps. They were better equipped, and we could not stand against them."''
([[VRRCPapaKhan.txt|Papa Khan's dialogue]])[[Courier]]: ''"What can you tell me about Freeside?"''
[[The King]]: ''"To understand Freeside, you have to look back a few years. Originally, we were all just tribes making a living in this area. That all changed when Mr. House came around. He made an offer to the three biggest tribes that were willing to listen to him. Today, everyone calls those tribes the Three Families, and they live in luxury and run their own casinos in the Strip. The rest of us were left to fight over the crumbs, living in the shadow of those more fortunate. Things got pretty nasty for a while. But we wanted more. A place of our own. ([[VFSTheKing.txt|The King's dialogue]]) House's consolidation of power came just in time for the arrival of the [[New California Republic Army]]'s advance forces, with House sending his Securitrons and tribal "employees" to occupy Hoover Dam as a show of force. This forced the NCR to negotiate with House as an independent power; in the end, the NCR agreed to recognize House's sovereignty over New Vegas in exchange for permission to use Hoover Dam and the defunct [[Camp McCarran|McCarran International Airport]] as military bases and divert 95% of the power and water generated by the dam for their own use, ensuring cooperation with the NCR in the near term. By [[Timeline#2281|2281]], House's efforts led to the establishment of New Vegas as a major power in the Mojave Wasteland through lucrative trade with the New California Republic and exploitation of the NCR's citizens as customers, guided by his aims to use the NCR's conflict with [[Caesar's Legion]] to further expand his control of the region. House continued to reside in the Lucky 38 and control the Securitrons as his envoys. At some point after emerging from stasis, House gambled with the residents of [[Vault 21]] for ownership of their Vault, followed by stripping it of all useful technology, and had planned to permanently seal the Vault away by filling it with cement.[[Sarah Weintraub]]: ''"All right! Please, follow me. We'll head into the vault right away. This bunker protects the entrance to the vault - solid stone outside and thick steel on the inside! Above us there's the control center for this level of the vault's life-support systems, electric grid, radioactive shields and all that jazz. Don't get lost! My vault has many corridors and rooms - although it is no longer symmetrical, after Mr. House threw us out. This is the main game-hall. Here we settled the big disputes among the vault's levels. Chosen representatives gambled against each other here. The winner earned the right to settle the dispute as wished by the collective. We used to have such parties in this diner! A bitch to clean later... but well worth it! This hall leads to our guest rooms. You can use the first room on our left. But no snooping next door! That's my room, always was. Down there is the game room! Each side of the vault had one... but the other is filled with concrete now. Okay, that wraps it up. I'll see you soon!"''
([[SarahWeintraub.txt|Sarah Weintraub's dialogue]]) However, House was convinced by [[Sarah Weintraub]] to leave the top section of Vault 21 intact and convert it into a hotel to serve visitors to the Strip.The [[Courier]]: ''"What does Mr. House have to do with Vault 21?"''
[[Sarah Weintraub]]: ''"Mr. House has everything to do with Vault 21. He tried to get us out before he filled it with concrete. I almost went ape! So, we convinced him - okay, Sheldon and I, right? We convinced him to leave the top level mostly intact!"''
([[SarahWeintraub.txt|Sarah Weintraub's dialogue]]) ====Recovering the platinum chip==== Even after bringing some of Vegas' luster back to the wasteland, Mr. House's top priority remained acquiring the platinum chip. For decades before the NCR's arrival, House spent cumulative millions of caps on scavenger teams and prospectors to dig it out of the ruins of [[Sunnyvale]], California, where it had been made.The [[Courier]]: ''"What do you know about the courier Benny shot?"''
[[Yes Man]]: ''"{{Tooltip|I knew {{Tooltip|he|Male}}/{{Tooltip|she|Female}} was carrying the Platinum Chip! And I knew right where Benny should wait for {{Tooltip|him|Male}}/{{Tooltip|her|Female}}! That's why Benny put me here! To monitor Mr. House's data transmissions. They're all encrypted, of course|{sunny} }} - {{Tooltip|but I'm quite a decrypter!|{swelling with pride} }} Did you know that Mr. House spent 812,545 caps hiring salvage teams to find the Platinum Chip- just in the last year alone? {{Tooltip|Of course you didn't!|{delighted} }} Or that there were seven couriers, but six of them were carrying junk? How about their exact routes, and the mercenary teams that screened them? I knew all that. Pretty smart, huh?"''
([[VMQTopsYesMan.txt|Yes Man's dialogue]]) This massive expenditure ultimately paid off in [[Timeline#2281|2281]] when the platinum chip was found after 204 years. Mr. House contracted the chip's delivery to the [[Mojave Express]]; to cover up the importance of the package, he arranged for a layered plot involving multiple couriers, most carrying packages with miscellaneous junk items to throw off potential risks,[[Mojave Express delivery order (6 of 6)]] and [[Mojave Express delivery order (4 of 6)]] additionally paying mercenary teams to screen the routes to be taken. Yet again, however, the platinum chip's delivery was halted. [[Courier|Courier Six]], the courier with the actual platinum chip, was intercepted by the Chairmen's leader and House's right-hand man, [[Benny]], around [[Goodsprings]] after Benny learned of the chip's existence and its route from the modified Securitron [[Yes Man]], who had backdoor access to House's datastream. Benny intended to leverage the chip to gain control of the Strip and make it an independent power in the wasteland, free of his employer's machinations.The [[Courier]]: ''"If the Chip's so valuable, why use a single courier to transport it?"''

Add to that many thousands of caps worth of mercenary protection to screen your avenue of approach. I didn't want to attract the attention of groups like the Great Khans or the Brotherhood of Steel. Alas, the real threat was closer to home."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) Though not initially aware of Benny's involvement, House learned the truth after a Securitron, [[Victor (Securitron)|Victor]], he had planted in Goodsprings reported the chip's theft back to him.The [[Courier]]: ''"Why didn't you intervene sooner when Benny ambushed me?"''

When he alerted me, I instructed him to approach the site after Benny and the others had departed.''"
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) Incensed at the betrayal, as he considered Benny a potential protégé, House nevertheless had to mask his knowledge of Benny's duplicity until the time came that he could act on it through a new agent.The [[Courier]]: ''"Tell me about Benny."''

Robert House: ''"To achieve my aims, I require a capable human agent to perform certain... {{Tooltip|tasks|choosing word}}. I knew Benny was ambitious, even ruthless. But in any case, you've come along - a more-than-suitable replacement."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) After learning through Victor that the Courier had survived and was making their way to the Strip, Mr. House began planning to invite them into the [[Lucky 38]] in hopes of using their desire for revenge on Benny to reclaim the platinum chip at long last.The [[Courier]]: ''"What terms are you offering?"''
Robert House: ''"My only concern is the recovery of the Platinum Chip. What happens to Benny, I leave to your discretion. When you bring the Chip to me, I will pay you four times the delivery bonus stipulated in your contract. How's that?"''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) In the event that the Courier proved reliable, House further sought to use them as his new agent to fully seize power over the Mojave amidst the upcoming [[Second Battle of Hoover Dam]]. ====2290s==== While the exact outcome of the Second Battle of Hoover Dam remains unclear, the New Vegas Strip also collapsed within this period, becoming overrun by [[Deathclaw (TV series)|deathclaws]]. ({{FOTV|2|8}}) Around July 2296, [[the Ghoul]] (Cooper Howard in his post-War persona) came to the Mojave Wasteland in pursuit of his wife's former assistant [[Hank MacLean]], whom he suspected was trying to get in touch with Robert House; the Ghoul suspected that his family may have survived in the management Vault underneath Las Vegas and believed that House was still alive and would be able to lead him to it. ({{FOTV|2|8}}) ===Personality=== {{Quotation|I have no interest in abusing others, just as I have no interest in legislating or otherwise dictating what people do in their private time. Nor have I any interest in being worshipped as some kind of machine god messiah. I am impervious to such corrupting ambitions. But autocracy? Firm control in the hands of a technological and economic visionary? Yes, that Vegas shall have.}} Mr. House is a very reclusive individual. Even in the pre-War era, he personally shunned overt public appearances, using a body double for all of his public affairs. Eventually, he became a total recluse, making him the subject of rumors; this may have been due to his integration into his life support technology shortly before the Great War. House remained just as reclusive after the Great War, never directly appearing in public even through a robotic medium and never allowing anyone into the Lucky 38. Mr. House seeks to restore [[New Vegas]] to its pre-War glory as a crown jewel of technological innovation and a bright neon paradise of business and fortune. Having experienced pre-War Vegas first-hand, he has long been enamored with the city's beauty and grandeur. His vision of autocracy and disillusionment with democratic society stems from his resentment towards the attitudes and actions of the increasingly desperate pre-War [[United States of America|United States]], whose decline was precipitated by the failure to adequately research and develop alternative [[Technology|technologies]]. His ultimate goal is to guide civilization's progress and forge a new future for mankind, free of the corrupting influences of the past. House's unwillingness to allow his life's work to be ruined by what he perceives as an increasingly unstable world has cemented, in his mind, the fate of democracy and human civilization itself. His contempt for most post-apocalyptic institutions, from bottle capsThe [[Courier]]: ''"I have a right to know more."''
Robert House: ''"That's simply not true. I am the only person to hold any rights pertaining to the Chip. I designed it, and I paid for it - dearly. To develop that Chip, I spent a sum of U.S. dollars - not the bottle caps that pass as currency these days - but a sum beyond counting. For decades, I paid salvagers to comb the ruins for it. And when it was finally discovered, tens of thousands of caps spent to have it brought here. We know how that turned out. Complete your contract and it will be the last time I pay for the Chip. Save your questions for then."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) to the various factions, stems from what he perceives as humanity's inability to learn from its past mistakes. His own strategies and decisions are largely based on mathematical calculations, and he is confident in his own ability to succeed.[[The House Always Wins]] He styles himself as an "autocrat," viewing [[New Vegas]] as his rightful dominion, and is dismissive of other factions vying for control, comparing them to "two snarling dogs fighting over a curve of bone." He further disparages both groups as nothing more than "regurgitations of the past" drawing parallels between the two as attempts to revive past civilizations rather than offer a palpable future. He derides the NCR as a "society of customers" led by scheming leaders who wish to take Vegas out from under him, while showing disgust at the Legion's practice of slavery, technophobia and general brutality.The [[Courier]]: ''"In the meantime, you'd rule Vegas as some kind of dictator?"''
Robert House: ''"I prefer the term "autocrat." I would rule as a chief executive. I would not answer to a board of directors or any other entity. Nothing to impede progress. If you want to see the fate of democracies, look out the windows."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) Nevertheless, he vastly prefers the NCR to the Legion, viewing the NCR as a possible long-term business partner while understanding that the Legion does not tolerate what they cannot control, and thus, while maintaining a facade of neutrality, actively plans for an NCR victory in the Mojave: just one on his terms with an Independent Vegas. Focused only on achieving his goals, he has little interest in monitoring or controlling the lives of others. He allows autonomy to the Three Families and is largely reliant on the information networks at his disposal and his Securitron patrols to maintain order. He takes pride in his achievements, seeing himself as a visionary. He also takes great interest in the Courier, seeing them as a valuable asset for overcoming obstacles too challenging for his other agents. Though their relationship is mainly professional, Mr. House comes to regard the Courier with respect and shows appreciation for their services, should they choose to help Mr. House. The Courier's success equates to his own success in judging them capable, inviting them to continue aiding him in his increasingly ambitious goals.The [[Courier]]: ''"Say you keep control of New Vegas. What happens next?"''
Robert House: ''"New Vegas is more than a city - it's the remedy to mankind's {{Tooltip|derailment|beat}}. The city's economy is a blast furnace in which can be forged the steel of a new rail line, running straight to a new horizon. What is the NCR? A society of people desperate to experience comfort, ease, luxury... A society of customers. With all that money pouring in? Give me 20 years, and I'll reignite the high technology development sectors. 50 years, and I'll have people in orbit. 100 years, and my colony ships will be heading for the stars, to search for planets unpolluted by the wrath and folly of a bygone generation."''

He's a laissez-faire dictator. "Do whatever you want as long as you don't cross me." Mr. House doesn't care about other people and what they do as long as Vegas remains prosperous and he remains in control.|[[Joshua Sawyer]]'s [[Joshua Sawyer Formspring posts/2011|Formspring on Robert House's ideology]]}} {{Quotation|[Question: ''Perhaps Mr. House is 'dictatorial' to the extent that he won't permit anyone to breach his quasi-governmental monopoly on force, but otherwise I'm not sure what you mean by 'laissez-faire dictator,' which seems like one heck of an oxymoron.'']

He's also authoritarian on economic issues within certain boundaries. In the same way that a fascist government would exert authority on the various production/capital resources involved in a market, Mr. House exerts his authority on The Strip's operation. Ultimately, he wants The Strip to be (extremely) profitable and to retain independence from NCR/CL. However, he does not want the families to be independent from his authority, so he does what he can to keep them under his thumb. He doesn't want to micromanage what they do, but he also knows that allowing them to do whatever they want could eventually lead to the downfall of his authority or fighting between the families (which would also undermine his authority).
Really, the main area in which Mr. House is "liberal" is in personal consumption and behavior. In this dialogue, House would have stated that he will not attack the player character if they simply walk away. {{FNVCC|end}} ===''Fallout'' TV series=== * {{Note|(Note 2)}} In the ''Fallout'' TV series, Robert House is played by actor [[Justin Theroux]], starting from the show's second season. This was explicitly confirmed in promotional materials and interviews for the show around the time of season 2's release.[https://archive.ph/eRVrF Gizmodo: "In 'Fallout' Season 2's First Trailer, All Roads Lead to New Vegas" (archived)] Meanwhile, [[Rafi Silver]] plays Mr. House's body double, who first appeared in the season 1 finale "[[The Beginning]]." However, within the show itself, Silver's character was credited as Robert House both in "The Beginning" and in the first episode of season 2, "[[The Innovator]];" he was first credited as the Robert House double in "[[The Wrangler]]." Theroux's character remains unnamed in the credits of all of the season 2 episodes he appears in, though the show itself confirms he is the actual Robert House. ** In an interview from December 2025, Geneva Robertson-Dworet and Justin Theroux alluded to the relationship between Theroux's House and Silver's House body double. Robertson-Dworet commented that this was based on Howard Hughes' increasing reclusiveness near the end of his life, stating that the writers wanted to depict House as someone "constantly playing tricks on the world" and "maybe somewhat scared to go out because, think of what a targeted man he is." Theroux suggested that House could have "become so paranoid, or so rarefied, that he needs to live above Las Vegas in a very protected place," also noting that the setting of the late 2070s made it "still possible to have avatars in the world where people wouldn't recognize [House]." * Prior to the release of season 2, Theroux's appearance as House was spotlighted in a ''GQ'' article. According to [[Geneva Robertson-Dworet]] and [[Jonathan Nolan]], the showrunners behind the TV series were interested in exploring House as a character, especially prior to the Great War. This interest was due to House himself being synonymous with Vegas, and they had already decided on going there as the primary setting of season 2. Additionally, they saw House's character as being relevant in the real world in 2025, at a time when "very wealthy technocrats have undue influence in the world," according to Nolan.[https://archive.ph/ZG0ma GQ: "First Look at Justin Theroux in ''Fallout'' Season 2: Inside the Show's Big Trip to Vegas" (archived)] ** Theroux was convinced to join the cast of ''Fallout''{{'}}s second season by [[Walton Goggins]], who is a close friend of Theroux. Theroux was already admired as an actor by Jonathan Nolan, who suggested to Goggins that he make the pitch. Prior to the offer, Theroux had neither seen the ''Fallout'' show nor played a ''Fallout'' game, but he accepted the offer and studied House's character by watching gameplay videos of ''Fallout: New Vegas'' on YouTube. According to Theroux, he believed Nolan saw real-world parallels in the present to the type of character House was, while Theroux himself personally interpreted House's character as being similar to [[wikipedia:Robert McNamara|Robert McNamara]], the real-world Secretary of Defense under [[wikipedia:John F. Kennedy|John F. Kennedy]] and [[wikipedia:Lyndon B. Johnson|Lyndon B. Johnson]], especially in relation to his prediction of nuclear threat at the height of the [[Cold War]]. Theroux also mentioned Howard Hughes as a reference point for his performance, reflecting how Hughes was cited as a significant influence for House's character as played by [[René Auberjonois]] during the original development of ''Fallout: New Vegas''. ** As other inspirations, Theroux also cited studying "radio announcers, newsmen and people who had [House's] specific dialect."[https://archive.ph/g9WiA Screen Rant: "Fallout Season 2: Justin Theroux On Taking Over Iconic Mr. House Role" (archived)] * After the release of "The Handoff," [[Geneva Robertson-Dworet]] said in an interview that a representation of Robert House powered by cold fusion seemed like the "ultimate version" of House. She explained that the writers viewed this as something it made sense for House, as a person interested in robotics and self-preservation, to develop, and that it also allowed the writers to include House in the story without overruling players' gameplay experiences in ''Fallout: New Vegas''. However, she declined to state whether this would be the "''final'' final form" of House in the series. * In a GQ interview following the release of "The Strip," Walton Goggins was asked how the scene between the Ghoul and Robert House's avatar in the Lucky 38 penthouse during "The Strip" was filmed.
